1. Introduction

AmplifyIQ respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store and protect personal information when you visit our website, contact us, request a quotation, become a client or otherwise interact with AmplifyIQ.

Contact AmplifyIQ:

Trading as AmplifyIQ County Mayo, Ireland Email: info@amplifyiq.ie

For the purposes of applicable data protection law, including the General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") and the Data Protection Act 2018, the above business is the data controller in relation to personal information collected for its own business purposes.

2. Information We May Collect

Depending on how you interact with us, we may collect the following categories of personal information.

Identity and Contact Information

This may include:

  • name;
  • business or organisation name;
  • email address;
  • telephone number;
  • postal or business address;
  • job title; and
  • other contact information you voluntarily provide.

Enquiry and Project Information

Where you contact us regarding a project or service, we may collect information including:

  • the services you are interested in;
  • information about your existing website;
  • project requirements;
  • business requirements;
  • messages and correspondence;
  • quotations requested;
  • project notes;
  • files or materials you send us; and
  • information required to prepare or perform a contract.

Client and Transaction Information

Where you become a client, we may process:

  • quotations;
  • proposals;
  • contracts;
  • invoices;
  • payment records;
  • project correspondence;
  • billing information;
  • records of services supplied; and
  • accounting and taxation records.

We do not normally store full payment-card details ourselves where payments are processed through a third-party payment provider.

Website and Technical Information

When you use our website, certain technical information may be collected automatically, including:

  • IP address;
  • browser type;
  • device type;
  • operating system;
  • approximate location derived from an IP address;
  • pages visited;
  • referral source;
  • session information;
  • website interaction information; and
  • cookie or similar technology identifiers.

Non-essential analytics or advertising technologies will only be activated where the required consent has been obtained.

3. How We Collect Personal Data

We may receive personal information:

  • directly from you;
  • through website contact or enquiry forms;
  • through email, telephone or social-media communications;
  • during consultations or project discussions;
  • when you request a quotation;
  • when you enter into an agreement with us;
  • when you make a payment;
  • through cookies and similar technologies where permitted;
  • through service providers acting on our behalf; or
  • from publicly available business sources where appropriate.

4. How We Use Personal Information

We may use personal information to:

  • respond to enquiries;
  • communicate with prospective clients;
  • prepare quotations or proposals;
  • provide web design, website redesign, digital growth and related services;
  • manage projects;
  • create and maintain client accounts and records;
  • issue invoices and process payments;
  • provide support;
  • manage hosting, domains or technical services where agreed;
  • improve our website and services;
  • maintain the security and performance of our website;
  • comply with accounting, taxation and legal obligations;
  • establish, exercise or defend legal claims;
  • prevent fraud or misuse;
  • manage our business relationship with clients and suppliers; and
  • send marketing communications where we have a lawful basis to do so.

5. Lawful Bases for Processing

Under GDPR, we must have a lawful basis for processing personal data.

Depending on the circumstances, we may rely upon the following bases.

Contract and Pre-Contractual Steps

We may process your information where necessary to:

  • provide a quotation;
  • discuss a proposed project;
  • enter into a contract with you; or
  • perform services under an existing contract.

Legal Obligation

We may process and retain information where required to comply with legal obligations including taxation, accounting and business-record requirements.

Legitimate Interests

We may process information where necessary for our legitimate business interests, provided those interests are not overridden by your rights and freedoms.

Such interests may include:

  • responding to business enquiries;
  • running and improving our business;
  • maintaining website and network security;
  • preventing fraud;
  • managing customer relationships;
  • protecting our legal rights; and
  • improving our services.

Consent

Where required, we rely on consent for activities such as:

  • non-essential cookies;
  • analytics technologies;
  • advertising or conversion-tracking technologies; and
  • certain forms of electronic marketing.

Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw that consent at any time.

Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing performed before consent was withdrawn.

6. Marketing Communications

We may send marketing communications where you have provided consent or where another lawful basis under applicable law allows us to do so.

Every electronic marketing communication sent by us will provide an appropriate method of unsubscribing.

You may also ask us to stop sending marketing communications at any time by contacting:

info@amplifyiq.ie

7. Cookies and Similar Technologies

Our website may use cookies, local storage, pixels and similar technologies.

Some technologies are necessary for the website to function correctly.

Other technologies, including analytics, advertising and conversion-tracking technologies, will only be used where the required consent has been obtained.

For detailed information, please see our Cookie Policy and use the control available on our website.

8. Sharing Personal Information

We do not sell personal information.

We may share information with trusted third parties where reasonably necessary to operate our business or provide services.

These may include:

  • hosting providers;
  • domain providers;
  • cloud infrastructure providers;
  • email providers;
  • website-development platforms;
  • analytics providers;
  • payment processors;
  • accounting or bookkeeping providers;
  • professional advisers;
  • contractors or subcontractors;
  • customer-relationship-management providers; and
  • other technology suppliers.

Where a third party processes personal information on our behalf, appropriate contractual and data-protection arrangements will be used where required.

We may also disclose information where required by law, regulation, court order or another lawful authority.

9. Client Data Processed on Behalf of Clients

During certain projects, AmplifyIQ may have access to personal data controlled by a client.

Examples may include:

  • website enquiry data;
  • customer databases;
  • mailing-list information;
  • website user information;
  • analytics information; or
  • information stored within a client's hosting environment.

Where AmplifyIQ processes personal data solely on a client's documented instructions, the client will generally act as the data controller and AmplifyIQ may act as a data processor.

Where required under GDPR, an appropriate Data Processing Agreement will be entered into between AmplifyIQ and the client.

10. International Data Transfers

Some technology suppliers used by AmplifyIQ or our clients may process information outside Ireland or the European Economic Area.

Where personal information is transferred internationally, we will seek to ensure an appropriate transfer mechanism and safeguards are used where required by applicable data-protection law.

These may include:

  • European Commission adequacy decisions;
  • Standard Contractual Clauses;
  • supplementary safeguards; or
  • another legally recognised transfer mechanism.

11. Data Retention

We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, including legal, accounting, contractual and dispute-resolution requirements.

Typical retention periods may include:

General enquiries

Enquiry information that does not result in a client relationship will normally be retained for up to 24 months after our last meaningful communication, unless a longer period is reasonably required.

Client and project information

Project and client information may be retained for the duration of the client relationship and afterwards where reasonably necessary for:

  • support;
  • warranty or service history;
  • contractual records;
  • intellectual-property records;
  • dispute resolution; or
  • legal claims.

Financial records

Invoices, payments, accounting information and associated business records may normally be retained for at least six years, or longer where required by law or necessary in connection with an ongoing matter.

Cookie consent records

Cookie-consent choices will be retained only for an appropriate period. Where applicable, users will be asked to reaffirm their choices periodically.

We may retain anonymised or aggregated information that no longer identifies an individual.

12. Security

We take reasonable technical and organisational measures designed to protect personal information from:

  • unauthorised access;
  • accidental loss;
  • misuse;
  • disclosure;
  • alteration; and
  • destruction.

However, no website, internet transmission or electronic storage system can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

13. Your Data Protection Rights

Subject to applicable law and any relevant exemptions, you may have the right to:

  • access personal data we hold about you;
  • request correction of inaccurate information;
  • request deletion of your personal information;
  • request restriction of processing;
  • object to certain processing;
  • receive certain personal information in a portable format;
  • withdraw consent where processing is based on consent; and
  • lodge a complaint with a data-protection supervisory authority.

To exercise your rights, contact:

info@amplifyiq.ie

We may need to verify your identity before acting on certain requests.

14. Complaints

If you have a concern regarding how AmplifyIQ processes your personal information, please contact us first at:

info@amplifyiq.ie

You also have the right to make a complaint to the Data Protection Commission of Ireland.

15. Third-Party Websites

Our website may contain links to websites operated by third parties.

AmplifyIQ is not responsible for the privacy practices or content of independent third-party websites.

You should review the privacy information provided by those websites before providing personal information.

16. Children's Privacy

AmplifyIQ's services are primarily intended for businesses and adult clients.

Our services are not intentionally directed at children, and we do not knowingly seek to collect personal information from children through our website.

17. Changes to this Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect:

  • changes to our services;
  • changes to technology;
  • changes to legal requirements; or
  • changes to how personal information is processed.

The latest version will be published on this page together with an updated revision date.

18. Contact

For questions regarding this Privacy Policy or the use of personal information, contact:

AmplifyIQ County Mayo, Ireland Email: info@amplifyiq.ie
